sections.content: Comparisons allow speakers to explain different ways of eating and living. Use *más*, *menos*, *tan* and tanto with *que* or *como*, and contrast ideas with *aunque*, *mientras* que and *sin* *embargo*. A B1 comparison should make the basis of the comparison clear.

items.spanish: La comida casera suele ser más barata que comer fuera, aunque requiere más tiempo.
items.english: Homemade food is usually cheaper than eating out, although it requires more time.

items.spanish: Una dieta vegetariana puede ser tan variada como una dieta que incluye carne.
items.english: A vegetarian diet can be as varied as a diet that includes meat.

items.spanish: Algunas personas consumen menos productos preparados, mientras que otras prefieren la comodidad.
items.english: Some people consume fewer prepared products, while others prefer convenience.

items.spanish: Comer fuera es cómodo; sin embargo, cocinar en casa me permite elegir los ingredientes.
items.english: Eating out is convenient; however, cooking at home allows me to choose the ingredients.

sections.content: Compare the same feature on both sides: price, time, variety or convenience. Use a contrast connector when the two ideas do not point in the same direction.
